subject: BlueHarbor integration: technical handoff & endpoint migration plan
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>

Subject: BlueHarbor integration: technical handoff & endpoint migration plan

Hi Alex —

Thanks for the productive kickoff earlier. Attached is the integration-runbook-v1.pdf and a small tarball with sample snippets that your engineers can run locally (redwood-sample-snippets.tar.gz). Below is a short, prioritized checklist to get the implementation moving and reduce surprises during the endpoint migration: 

1) Sandbox access + sample traffic
   - We will provision a sandbox token and a temporary sandbox endpoint (/v1/sandbox/generate) by EOD Mon.
   - Please send the primary engineer email so we can add them to the sandbox ACL.

2) SDK quickstart and runtime expectations
   - Use the official Redwood JS SDK (v1.4+). Minimal example included in the tarball (node/index.js).
   - Default recommended timeouts: connect=2s, request=20s for chat/generation.
   - Retry/backoff: exponential with jitter; base delay 250ms, max 5s, attempts up to 4 for idempotent calls.

3) Rate limiting and traffic shaping
   - We expose X-RateLimit-Limit and X-RateLimit-Remaining headers on responses. We recommend a client-side token bucket with burst window=2x baseline.
   - For initial rollout, we'll cap production traffic to 30% of expected QPS for 48 hours.

4) Endpoint migration plan (high level)
   - Canary: switch 10% traffic for 6 hours, monitor latency, error rates, and token usage.
   - Full switch: DNS CNAME change to the v2 endpoint during a 2-hour maintenance window; rollback within 30 minutes if errors spike.

Next steps (action items):
- Alex: share eng contact + preferred maintenance window (week of 11/24?)
- BlueHarbor procurement: confirm PO terms; Stephanie will share license_amendment_blueharbor.docx for signature.
- Redwood: Vanessa will schedule a 60-minute handoff session with the integration engineers.

Attached: integration-runbook-v1.pdf, redwood-sample-snippets.tar.gz, license_amendment_blueharbor.docx

Thanks — looking forward to the rollout.

—
Stephanie Nguyen

Alex — great, we will: 

- Provision sandbox token for jules.park@blueharbor.com today and send a separate secure link with the token (do not paste tokens in email).
- cURL example: your snippet is correct; the final generated sandbox URL will be https://api.sandbox.redwood.ai/v1/sandbox/generate. Replace SANDBOX_TOKEN with the secure token we send.

Here are a few concrete SDK tips I asked the duo to add to the runbook: 

• JS SDK minimal (example from redwood-sample-snippets):

const Redwood = require('@redwoodai/sdk');
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_KEY, timeout: 20000 });
(async () => {
  try {
    const res = await client.generate({ model: 'redwood-rl-1', input: 'Ping' });
    console.log(res.output);
  } catch (err) {
    // retry logic should only run for network / 5xx; do not retry on 4xx client errors
    console.error('invoke failed', err.message);
  }
})();

• Retry guidance:
  - Only retry idempotent calls (embeddings, sync rerank). For generation/chat, prefer client-side validation to avoid repeated costly token generation.
  - Backoff: base=250ms, multiplier=2, jitter=random(0,100ms), maxAttempts=4.
  - For 429 responses, respect Retry-After if present; otherwise use exponential backoff and drop to a 429-slow-path if repeated.

• Timeouts & streaming:
  - Streaming responses can keep connections open; set a 120s read timeout for streaming endpoints, and implement a ping/keepalive to detect broken connections in load balancers.

Schedule proposal: Vanessa will run the 60-min handoff on 2025-11-24 10:00 PST. Can you confirm Jules and one engineer (name + email) for that session?

I'll upload a short checklist to the Drive link and mark items as complete as we go.

—
Stephanie

Alex / team — quick technical notes from the runtime side before the handoff call: 

- Batching / KV cache: if you enable parallel requests for multi-turn chat, set KV cache affinity per session id to avoid cross-session cache thrash. Default affinity key should be user_id or conversation_id.

- Migration steps (detailed):
  1) Prep: run smoke tests against sandbox for 48 hours with production-like payloads (we can extend sandbox quota for you).
  2) Canary: route 10% of production traffic to v2 endpoint for 6h. Watch P50/P95/P99 latencies and 5xx ratio.
  3) Scale: after 24h with stable metrics, move to 50% for 12h.
  4) Cutover: during a 2-hour window, update CNAME from api.blueharbor.com -> prod-v2.redwood.ai. Have a DNS TTL of 60s beforehand.
  5) Rollback: if error rate >1% or latency P95 increases >300ms vs baseline, revert CNAME and abort until root cause found.

- Rollout safeguards: set client-side soft-limit at 70% of expected QPS and implement server-error circuit (open for 60s after 5xx surge) before automatic retries.

- Observability knobs we'll provide for the handoff session: token-level cost breakdown, per-route latency histograms, and a short query to detect token-usage regressions.

Action: Alex — please confirm engineering contacts for access. I'll add the required runtime dashboards to the Drive folder once we have the engineer list.

Thanks,
